predecessors.note: From 192 on the History of Fujian's reading: Wuzhu's Minyue held southern Zhejiang ('His kingdom extended beyond the borders of contemporary Fujian into eastern Guangdong, eastern Jiangxi, and southern Zhejiang.' (History of Fujian)), and Wenzhou and Taizhou lie inside it, so the land comes from Minyue (minyue ledger: split 192, counterpart dong-ou). The Dong'ou page says only that Emperor Gaozu gave the realm to Zou Yao in 192; the Minyue page: 'and in 192 BC, he made Zou Yao king of Dong'ou (Eastern Ou).' That the land had been Minyue's is my reading, not a sentence of either page.

land.text: Dong'ou, 'an ancient kingdom in modern Wenzhou and Taizhou, Zhejiang Province, China' (Dong'ou page)

successors.note: Han absorbs the kingdom in 138: 'During the Han campaigns against Minyue in 138 BC, the king of Dong'ou no longer wished to live in his realm' ... 'to have him and his people's eventual fates to be absorbed into the Han empire.' (Dong'ou page). The infobox's 'Annexed by the Han dynasty: 111 BC' is recorded as a disagreement (see dong-ou ledger 138). No page names a Han commandery for Wenzhou or Taizhou (the Kuaiji Commandery page is silent).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 192-138: Cliopatria has no Dong'ou row. The page places the state only in 'an ancient kingdom in modern Wenzhou and Taizhou, Zhejiang Province, China' and names the capital Dong'ou (modern Wenzhou); it gives no area and no frontier, so two discs of 70 km and 50 km stand for the two prefectures, the researcher's reading (78 cells, about 19,700 km2). The Minyue Cliopatria shapes (Fujian) end south of this land, and the corrected Minyue shapes (minyue_-192 on) carve these discs out of southern Zhejiang. The 138 submission to Han is the only border event.

ledger.note: 192: Emperor Gaozu of Han gives the realm of Dong'ou to Zou Yao. 'The realm of Dong'ou was given to Zou Yao by Emperor Gaozu of Han in 192 BC' (Dong'ou page; the infobox says 'Established: 191 BC'); the Minyue page: 'and in 192 BC, he made Zou Yao king of Dong'ou (Eastern Ou).' The land is Wenzhou and Taizhou, named by the page; the outline is the researcher's. It lies inside the southern Zhejiang that the History of Fujian gives to Wuzhu's Minyue ('His kingdom extended beyond the borders of contemporary Fujian into eastern Guangdong, eastern Jiangxi, and southern Zhejiang.' (History of Fujian)), so it is drawn as split from Minyue (minyue ledger 192); the Dong'ou page itself does not say where the land came from.

ledger.note: 138: a Han fleet makes Minyue withdraw. The Emperor Wu page: the Kuaiji governor was coerced 'to mobilize a large naval fleet to Dong'ou's rescue' and 'Minyue forces became fearful and retreated'; the Dong'ou infobox says 'Defeated by Minyue: 138 BC' and the text has the Dong'ou king submit to Han. The pages do not say that land changed hands.

region.text: Dong'ou, 'an ancient kingdom in modern Wenzhou and Taizhou, Zhejiang Province, China' (Dong'ou page)

ledger.note: 138: the king of Dong'ou submits to Han and the kingdom passes to Han. 'During the Han campaigns against Minyue in 138 BC, the king of Dong'ou no longer wished to live in his realm' ... 'having submitted himself in an prostrating gesture' ... 'to have him and his people's eventual fates to be absorbed into the Han empire.' (Dong'ou page). The Baiyue page has the king ask to move his people into Han territory, and they 'settled in the region between the Yangtze and Huai River'. The infobox's 'Annexed by the Han dynasty: 111 BC' is a disagreement: the page's 111 paragraph is about Dongyue and the former Minyue ('the aspiration for autonomous control over Dongyue gradually dissipated during the final months of 111 BC'), the infobox ruler list stops in 138 and no page says Dong'ou held Wenzhou or Taizhou after 138 (the Kuaiji Commandery page is silent). Confidence 2: the year and the submission are the page's; that the land passed to Han at once, when the page says 'eventual', is my reading.

notes:
Written by the Minyue researcher (ea-01-e) as a direct counterpart that no Cliopatria row covers; repaired in a second pass after the review. Pages: the Dong'ou article (read three times), the Emperor Wu of Han page, the Minyue page and the History of Fujian page; second pass also Baiyue and Kuaiji Commandery. Dong'ou is not on Cliopatria. Wikidata id unknown (null; wikidata.org is unreachable).

END, CHANGED FROM 111 TO 138 (review finding 1). The Dong'ou page's text: 'During the Han campaigns against Minyue in 138 BC, the king of Dong'ou no longer wished to live in his realm' ... 'having submitted himself in an prostrating gesture' ... 'to have him and his people's eventual fates to be absorbed into the Han empire.' The infobox ruler list stops in 138 ('138–138 BCE: Wang (望)'), and the infobox says both 'Defeated by Minyue: 138 BC' and 'Annexed by the Han dynasty: 111 BC'. The page's 111 paragraph is about Dongyue and the former Minyue ('the aspiration for autonomous control over Dongyue gradually dissipated during the final months of 111 BC'; 'prompting the Han dynasty to eventually incorporate Dongyue and the remaining territories of the former Minyue'), not about Dong'ou. I take 138 (loss and dissolve, counterpart han-dynasty, confidence 2) and keep the infobox's 111 as a recorded disagreement in the ledger notes and here. The first pass had put the Dongyue sentence in the loss note as Dong'ou's annexation; it is gone. The Baiyue page agrees with 138: the Dong'ou king asked to move his people into Han territory and they 'settled in the region between the Yangtze and Huai River'. Not found on any page: who held Wenzhou and Taizhou after 138 (Kuaiji Commandery page silent; the Emperor Wu page resettles 'the people of Dang'an' without naming Dong'ou), so the land is given to Han and no commandery is named. A reviewer who prefers 111 needs a page that says Dong'ou held Wenzhou and Taizhou after 138.

START. 192 (lead and text: given to Zou Yao by Gaozu) against 191 (infobox 'Established: 191 BC' and 'Yao (搖) 191–185 BCE'). 192 is used and the first reign now starts in 192 with a note. The 192 land: the found event and the predecessors now name minyue as the source (History of Fujian puts southern Zhejiang in Wuzhu's kingdom; Wenzhou and Taizhou lie in it), mirroring minyue's 192 split (counterpart dong-ou). That the land was Minyue's is my reading of the History of Fujian; the Dong'ou page does not say it.

NOT ON THE PAGE: area, frontier, resettlement of Dong'ou by name on the Emperor Wu page. Two discs (Wenzhou 70 km, Taizhou 50 km; 78 cells) stand for the page's 'modern Wenzhou and Taizhou'. The location quote is now word for word: 'an ancient kingdom in modern Wenzhou and Taizhou, Zhejiang Province, China'. Taizhou is ambiguous in the gazetteer so a coordinate is used. Mirrors owed: han-dynasty gain 138 (counterpart dong-ou); minyue holds the other side of the 192 split and the 138 contest.
